plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to zero for capital preservation.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a potential return of around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating all leveraged ETFs and trimming concentrated positions. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single name concentration limit.
Reduce exposure to leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to small allocations.
Introduce VRT as a new position, leveraging a strong scanner setup.
This plan balances risk and growth, aiming for a more diversified portfolio.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for a potential return of around 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality scanner setup. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a focus on sustainable growth.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single name concentration limit.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to press working themes.
Introduce VRT as a new position, leveraging a strong scanner setup.
This plan aims for aggressive growth by leaning into leverage and high-scoring setups.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets a potential return of around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring scanner setups. Be aware that this approach carries substantially higher risk, including larger potential drawdowns and the impact of leveraged ETF decay/rebalancing.

plan: Sell all high-beta and leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to near zero.
Increase QQQI allocation to 30% to prioritize steady monthly distributions.
This plan focuses on generating reliable income and reducing growth-oriented risk.
It aims for a low-drawdown profile suitable for parking cash for yield.
income.read: This income plan targets a potential return of around 1% per month, prioritizing yield and capital stability. It significantly reduces exposure to high-beta and leveraged assets, focusing on income-generating ETFs. While aiming for steady distributions, remember that NAV can still fall in market downturns, and distributions are not guaranteed.
